classification.difficultyReason: Infer the rectangle length from the total length and quadrant radius, then add the rectangle and quadrant areas exactly.

content.prompt: Find the area of the figure shown below, leaving your answer in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: Unshaded rectangle on the left joined to a quadrant on the right. The dashed vertical join is a radius labelled 9 cm. The complete bottom edge has a 20 cm dimension arrow. Right-angle markers occur at the rectangle's top-left and bottom-left corners and at the foot of the dashed radius.
spec.mathematics: The quadrant has centre at the foot of the dashed join and radius 9 cm. Its horizontal radius forms the rightmost portion of the total 20 cm base. The rectangle therefore has height 9 cm and length 20−9 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied dimensions and marks are visible; inferred lengths and areas are absent.

answer.short:
$\left(99+\dfrac{81\pi}{4}\right)\text{ cm}^2$

Add the rectangle area to one quarter of the circle area.
answer.worked:
The curved part is a quadrant of radius $9\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Rectangle length}&=20-9\\\text{Rectangle length}&=11\text{ cm}\\\text{Rectangle area}&=11\times9\\\text{Rectangle area}&=99\text{ cm}^2\\\text{Quadrant area}&=\frac14\times\pi\times9^2\\\text{Quadrant area}&=\frac{81\pi}{4}\text{ cm}^2\\\text{Total area}&=\left(99+\frac{81\pi}{4}\right)\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
